original_excerpt:
From De Jonge v. Oregon, 299 U.S. 353, 364–365 (1937):
"The right of peaceable assembly is a right cognate to those of free speech and free press and is equally fundamental... The holding of meetings for peaceable political action cannot be proscribed."
From Tinker v. Des Moines Independent Community School District, 393 U.S. 503, 506, 513 (1969):
"It can hardly be argued that either students or teachers shed their constitutional rights to freedom of speech or expression at the schoolhouse gate... conduct by the student, in class or out of it, which for any reason—whether it stems from time, place, or type of behavior—materially disrupts classwork or involves substantial disorder or invasion of the rights of others is, of course, not immunized by the constitutional guarantee of freedom of speech."
attribution: De Jonge and Tinker majority opinions
fidelity: Both quoted components correspond with marked internal ellipses; De Jonge second component remains on 365.
scope_note: Peaceable lawful political assembly and school speech subject to disruption/disorder/rights-of-others limits. Listed Barnette/Shelton/Edwards are not independently authenticated by these Column N quotes.
